the hook called at every selection, and the permutation check over its return
the filing times the context carries

the passthrough and the context's shape

summary: Chain.order reorders the pickable work entries at every selection over an OrderContext the engine already holds, and a return that is not a permutation refuses the tick naming the hook
acceptance: a declared order decides which pickable work entry a tick picks; a return that drops, adds or repeats an entry refuses the tick naming the hook, before any agent runs; the context carries the whole queue, the resolved blockedBy graph, each entry's filing time and the entries in flight
tests: a declared order decides which pickable entry a tick picks
the order hook is handed only pickable work entries
OrderContext carries the whole queue, including groups and steps
OrderContext carries the blockedBy graph resolved over the queue, each entry's filing time and the entries in flight
an order that drops a pickable entry refuses the tick naming the hook
an order that returns an entry it was not handed refuses the tick naming the hook
an order that repeats an entry refuses the tick naming the hook
a non-permutation refuses before any agent runs
pins: an undeclared order leaves the default filing order standing
notes: Pure and synchronous like `shipped`, so a test drives it without a tick. It orders and never admits: the engine's own holds — gate, quarantine, claim, refusesEntry — are settled before the hook sees the set.
